title: The Bald Huntsman
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Man who had lost all his hair took to wearing a wig, and one day he went out hunting. It was blowing rather hard at the time, and he hadn't gone far before a gust of wind caught his hat and carried it off, and his wig too, much to the amusement of the hunt. But he quite entered into the joke, and said, "Ah, well! the hair that wig is made of didn't stick to the head on which it grew; so it's no wonder it won't stick to mine."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Man start wearing a wig?
options: He had lost all his hair
He wanted to disguise himself while hunting
It was the fashion among huntsmen
His hat no longer fit without one

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what activity was the Man doing when the incident happened?
options: Hunting
Riding to a market
Attending a wedding
Walking home from church

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the weather like at the time?
options: It was blowing rather hard
It was raining heavily
It was perfectly calm
Snow was beginning to fall

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the gust of wind carry off?
options: His hat and his wig
His hat only
His cloak and his hat
His wig and his gloves

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the hunt react to the Man losing his hat and wig?
options: With amusement
With alarm for his safety
With complete indifference
By stopping the hunt entirely

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Man say about why the wig wouldn't stick to his head?
options: Because the hair never stuck to the head it originally grew on, either
Because his head was too small for the wig
Because he had never worn it properly fastened
Because the wind that day was unusually strong

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Man's reaction to losing his wig reveal about his character?
options: He can laugh at his own misfortune instead of feeling humiliated by it
He is secretly furious but hides his anger from the hunt
He blames the wind for ruining an expensive purchase
He no longer wishes to go hunting after the incident

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Meeting one's own misfortune with good humour can turn a joke against oneself into no disgrace at all
Wigs should never be worn while hunting outdoors
Baldness is a source of shame that cannot be joked about
It is unwise to hunt on a windy day

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how far had the Man gone before the incident occurred?
options: Not far
Several miles
All the way home
To the edge of the forest

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Man respond to the joke made at his expense?
options: He quite enters into the joke himself
He storms off in embarrassment
He accuses the hunt of mocking him
He refuses to speak for the rest of the day

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Man say it's no wonder about?
options: That the wig won't stick to his own head
That the wind is so strong today
That the hunt found the accident funny
That his hat blew off before the wig did

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what comparison does the Man draw to explain the wig's failure to stay on his head?
options: He compares his own head to the head the hair originally grew on, which the hair also failed to stay attached to
He compares the wig to his hat, which was also poorly made
He compares his misfortune to that of other hunters
He compares the wind that day to a wind from years earlier

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "amusement" mean in "much to the amusement of the hunt"?
options: Enjoyment or entertainment at something funny
Sudden fear or alarm
Deep sympathy for someone's loss
Confusion about what had happened

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A gust of wind blows off a bald Man's hat and wig, and he jokes that the hair never stuck to its own original head either
A Man loses his hat during a hunt and blames the wind for ruining his trip
A Man's wig is stolen by another hunter as a prank
A Man refuses to wear a wig again after it embarrasses him publicly
